claims.statement: Reverting from v18 to v17 did not resolve the held orders; the 186 original orders remain held AND new east-node allocations under v17 logic are also held, indicating the problem is not v18-specific
claims.limitation: Conclusively rules out v18 as root cause; problem is universal to east-node routing regardless of allocation rule version

claims.statement: The root cause is a carrier feed lag on the east-node carrier: the east-node carrier is not picking up ANY orders routed there (both v18 split-reservation orders and orders from v17 allocations), indicating a systemic carrier availability or feed issue rather than an allocation-rule incompatibility
claims.corroboration: v18 revert failed to resolve the issue (m8_r_revert); dock capacity is normal (m8_r_dock); all affected orders route to east node (m8_r_exceptions); problem is universal to east-node routing, not v18-specific
claims.limitation: Specific carrier feed identity and exact lag duration not confirmed; must trace handoffs or inspect partition offsets to pinpoint the carrier feed mechanism

next_action.rationale: The revert attempt revealed that the problem is not v18-specific but a systemic east-node carrier issue. All orders routed to east node remain held regardless of allocation rule version. Tracing cohort handoffs for the EXC-0921 scope will show exactly where these orders are stuck in the system: still queued to the east-node carrier feed (indicating carrier_feed_lag), or stuck earlier in the allocation/pickup-scheduling pipeline (indicating a different mechanism). This will confirm whether the fix is a carrier-side slot correction or if there's a deeper system issue.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Will reveal where in the fulfillment pipeline the east-node orders are actually stuck and whether they have reached the carrier feed at all. This discriminates between carrier_feed_lag (stuck waiting for carrier pickup) vs. other system-level issues.
